Edges offered: | edge | |---| | mis:integer_division->AllDoublesToAvoidDivision | wrong rule: Making every variable a double is the right fix for integer division. | right rule: Use int for countable things and double for measured ones; where a fraction is needed, make one operand of the division a double (or cast) instead of changing every type. | | mis:integer_division->CastAfterIntDivision | wrong rule: (double) (3 / 5) is 0.6. | right rule: The integer division 3 / 5 = 0 happens before the cast, so the result is 0.0. | | mis:integer_division->IntegerDivisionGivesFraction | wrong rule: 10 / 3 evaluates to 3.333.... | right rule: Dividing two ints gives an int: the fractional part is discarded. | | mis:integer_division->LaterDoubleLiteralFixesDivision | wrong rule: Changing a later literal to 100.0 fixes an earlier int division. | right rule: The int division happens first; the double must be in the division itself. | | mis:integer_division->NegativeRemainderSign | wrong rule: a % b is never negative, and integer division of a negative number rounds down. | right rule: a / b rounds toward 0 and a % b takes the sign of a: -14 / 3 is -4 and -14 % 3 is -2. | | mis:integer_division->TargetTyping | wrong rule: The type of a numerical expression depends on the type expected by the surrounding context, so double d = a / b; keeps the fraction. | right rule: The type of a numerical expression is determined by the expression, so double d = a / b; with int a and b still divides as ints. |
